domains.name: Compute
domains.subtitle: EC2 · Lambda · ECS · EKS · Elastic Beanstalk · Batch · Lightsail

services.name: Amazon EC2
services.desc: Virtual servers (instances) in the cloud. Foundation of AWS compute.
examTopics: Instance types: General (t3, m5), Compute (c5), Memory (r5), Storage (i3), Accelerated (p3, g4)
Purchasing options: On-Demand, Reserved (1yr/3yr, Standard/Convertible), Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Savings Plans
AMI: regional, can be shared, used for launch
User Data: runs at first launch (bootstrap scripts)
Metadata: 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
Instance Store vs EBS: ephemeral vs persistent
Placement Groups: Cluster (low-latency), Spread (max AZ separation), Partition (distributed)
ENI (Elastic Network Interface): can attach/move between instances
Elastic IP: static public IP
Hibernate: RAM saved to EBS, faster restart
Nitro: newer hypervisor, better performance, bare metal support
Spot: up to 90% off, 2-minute interruption notice; use Spot Fleet + capacity-optimized allocation for fault-tolerant/batch work
Savings Plans: Compute (flexible across EC2/Fargate/Lambda) vs EC2 Instance (cheaper, family/region locked)
uses: Host web apps, APIs, or any custom workload needing full server control
Run compute-intensive jobs like video rendering or data processing
services.tip: Know On-Demand vs Reserved vs Spot vs Savings Plans. EC2 is IaaS.

services.name: EC2 Auto Scaling
services.desc: Automatically adjusts EC2 fleet size based on demand.
examTopics: Launch Template vs Launch Configuration (Templates preferred, support versioning)
Scaling policies: Target Tracking, Step, Simple, Scheduled
Cooldown period: default 300s, prevents rapid scaling
Lifecycle hooks: pause during launch/terminate for custom actions
Mixed instance policy: combine On-Demand + Spot
Health checks: EC2 health vs ELB health
Min / Max / Desired capacity

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.desc: Serverless function execution — pay per invocation.
examTopics: Max execution: 15 minutes
Memory: 128 MB – 10 GB (CPU scales with memory)
Triggers: API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB Streams, SQS, SNS, CloudWatch Events/EventBridge
Concurrency: default 1000/region (soft limit), reserved vs provisioned
Cold Start: first invocation latency (use provisioned concurrency to avoid)
Layers: shared code/libraries across functions
Deployment package: ZIP or container image (up to 10 GB)
Environment variables (can be encrypted with KMS)
VPC configuration: needs NAT if requires internet access
uses: Event-driven microservices triggered by S3 uploads or API calls
Real-time data transformation in serverless architectures
services.tip: Serverless = no server management. Max 15 min timeout. Pay per invocation.

services.name: Elastic Beanstalk
services.desc: PaaS — deploy web apps without managing infrastructure.
examTopics: Supports: Java, .NET, PHP, Node, Python, Ruby, Go, Docker
Manages: EC2, ASG, ELB, RDS, monitoring automatically
Deployment modes: All at once, Rolling, Rolling with additional batch, Immutable, Blue/Green
Not truly serverless — EC2 instances under the hood
.ebextensions: customize configuration via YAML files

services.name: AWS Batch
services.desc: Run batch computing jobs at any scale (HPC/scientific).
examTopics: Managed EC2 or Spot instances under the hood
Job Queue → Job Definition → Compute Environment
Use for: ETL, genomics, financial modelling
Difference from Lambda: no time limit, can use Docker containers
uses: Overnight financial risk model computations
Large-scale ML training data preprocessing

services.name: Amazon Lightsail
services.desc: Simplified VPS — predictable pricing for small workloads.
examTopics: Includes compute, storage, DNS, static IP bundled
Good for: blogs, simple websites, dev environments
Not integrated deeply with other AWS services
Exam trap: choose Lightsail for simple/predictable workloads, EC2 for scalable ones
uses: Simple WordPress or small web app hosting
Affordable dev/test environments with predictable billing

services.name: AWS Outposts
services.desc: AWS hardware in your on-premises data center for hybrid workloads.
examTopics: Same APIs, tools, and hardware as AWS cloud
Owned/operated by AWS, installed on-premises
Use when: data residency, low latency to on-prem, local processing required
Supports EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, ECS, EKS on Outposts
uses: Factory floor manufacturing apps needing single-digit ms latency to local machines
Regulated workloads requiring data to never leave a specific physical location
services.tip: Outposts = AWS IN YOUR DATA CENTER. WaveLength = AWS IN 5G TELECOM. Ground Station = AWS FOR SATELLITES.

comparisons.title: EC2 Purchasing Options — When to Use Each

callouts.title: 🪤 Common Exam Traps — Compute
items: Spot vs Reserved: Spot for batch/flexible workloads, Reserved for steady-state databases
Lambda limit: 15-minute max — anything longer needs EC2/ECS/Batch
Elastic Beanstalk ≠ Serverless — it runs EC2 instances under the hood
Instance Store data is LOST on stop/terminate — not suitable for persistent data
Placement Group — Cluster: same AZ, NOT multi-AZ — NOT highly available

domains.name: Storage
domains.subtitle: S3 · EBS · EFS · FSx · Storage Gateway · AWS Backup

services.name: Amazon S3
services.desc: Object storage. Unlimited capacity, 11 9s durability.
examTopics: Storage Classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible, Glacier Deep Archive
Max object size: 5 TB; multipart upload required >100MB, mandatory >5GB
Versioning: protect against accidental delete/overwrite
Replication: CRR (cross-region), SRR (same-region) — versioning must be enabled
Encryption: SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, SSE-C, client-side
Access: Bucket Policy (resource-based), ACL (legacy), IAM (identity-based)
Pre-signed URLs: time-limited access for unauthenticated users
Static website hosting (no HTTPS natively — use CloudFront)
Transfer Acceleration: uses CloudFront edge for faster upload
S3 Select: query data inside objects with SQL
Event Notifications → SNS / SQS / Lambda / EventBridge
Object Lock: WORM compliance (Governance / Compliance mode)
Requester Pays: requester pays data transfer costs
MFA Delete: requires MFA to permanently delete versions
uses: Host static websites and store media assets globally
Data lake for analytics workloads like Athena queries
services.tip: Know S3 storage classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible, Deep Archive. Also know versioning, bucket policies.

services.name: Amazon EBS
services.desc: Block storage volumes attached to EC2. Like a network hard drive.
examTopics: Types: gp3 (default SSD), io2/io1 (high IOPS, critical DBs), st1 (HDD, throughput), sc1 (HDD, cold)
AZ-locked — cannot attach to EC2 in another AZ directly
Snapshots: incremental, stored in S3, can copy cross-region
Encryption: encrypted at rest and in transit; encrypted AMI → encrypted EBS
Multi-Attach: io1/io2 can attach to multiple EC2 in same AZ
gp3 vs gp2: gp3 allows independent IOPS/throughput provisioning, cheaper
Delete on termination: default ON for root volume
gp3 decouples capacity from IOPS/throughput (set them independently); gp2 coupled IOPS to volume size
Instance Store: ephemeral local disk, data lost on stop/terminate — never for persistent data

services.name: Amazon EFS
services.desc: Managed NFS — shared file system for Linux instances.
examTopics: Multi-AZ — can mount to multiple EC2 simultaneously
Linux only (NFS protocol)
Storage tiers: Standard and EFS-IA (Infrequent Access)
Performance modes: General Purpose vs Max I/O
Throughput modes: Bursting vs Provisioned
EFS vs EBS: EFS = shared/Linux, EBS = single instance/any OS
uses: Shared storage for a fleet of web servers serving the same content
Content management systems (WordPress, Drupal) on multiple servers
services.tip: EFS = shared Linux NFS. FSx for Windows = SMB/Windows shares. S3 = object storage.

services.name: Amazon FSx
services.desc: Fully managed third-party file systems.
examTopics: FSx for Windows File Server: SMB, Active Directory, Windows-based workloads
FSx for Lustre: HPC, ML, financial modelling, integrates with S3
FSx for NetApp ONTAP: multi-protocol (NFS/SMB/iSCSI)
FSx for OpenZFS: Linux/BSD workloads
Key trap: Windows shared storage → FSx for Windows (NOT EFS)
uses: Lift Windows-based file shares to the cloud without re-architecting
HPC workloads (genomics, simulation) needing ultra-fast parallel storage

services.name: AWS Storage Gateway
services.desc: Hybrid cloud storage bridge between on-premises and AWS.
examTopics: S3 File Gateway: NFS/SMB → S3 (caches locally)
FSx File Gateway: SMB/Windows → FSx
Volume Gateway (Cached): iSCSI, primary in S3, cache on-prem
Volume Gateway (Stored): iSCSI, primary on-prem, async backup to S3
Tape Gateway: Virtual Tape Library → S3/Glacier (replace physical tapes)
uses: Transparently back up on-prem data to S3 without changing apps
Extend on-prem storage seamlessly to the cloud

services.name: AWS Backup
services.desc: Centralized backup management for AWS services.
examTopics: Supports: EC2, EBS, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3, Outposts
Backup plans: schedule, retention, lifecycle to cold storage
Cross-region & cross-account backup support
Vault Lock: WORM — prevent deletion by anyone

callouts.title: 🪤 S3 vs EBS vs EFS Comparison
items: S3: Object storage, internet-accessible, not mountable as file system, used for backups/static files/media
EBS: Block storage, one EC2 at a time (except io2 Multi-Attach), AZ-specific, high performance
EFS: File storage, shared across many EC2 instances, multi-AZ, Linux only, higher cost

comparisons.title: EBS gp3 vs io2 vs Instance Store

domains.name: Databases
domains.subtitle: RDS · Aurora · DynamoDB · ElastiCache · Redshift · Neptune · DocumentDB

services.name: Amazon RDS
services.desc: Managed relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, MSSQL).
examTopics: Multi-AZ: synchronous replication, automatic failover, NOT for read scaling
Read Replicas: asynchronous, up to 5 per DB, used for read scaling
Read Replicas can be cross-region (charges for data transfer)
Automated backups (0–35 days retention) + manual snapshots
Encryption: must be enabled at creation; encrypted source → encrypted replica
Storage: gp2/gp3/io1, auto-scaling supported
RDS Proxy: pooling connections, improves Lambda scalability
IAM authentication: MySQL, PostgreSQL
Maintenance window: scheduled downtime for updates
uses: E-commerce product catalog and order management systems
Enterprise apps needing ACID-compliant SQL databases
services.tip: RDS = managed but not serverless. Multi-AZ = high availability. Read Replicas = performance.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.desc: AWS-optimized relational DB — 5x MySQL, 3x PostgreSQL performance.
examTopics: 6 copies of data across 3 AZs (storage auto-heals)
Up to 15 Read Replicas (vs 5 for RDS), sub-10ms lag
Aurora Global Database: cross-region, <1 sec replication lag
Aurora Serverless v2: auto-scales capacity (ACUs), great for variable workloads
Backtrack: roll back DB without restore (within hours)
Multi-Master: write to multiple instances simultaneously
Cluster endpoint, reader endpoint, custom endpoint
uses: High-throughput SaaS apps needing MySQL/PostgreSQL compatibility
Replacing costly Oracle licenses with a cloud-native alternative

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.desc: Fully managed NoSQL key-value/document database. Serverless.
examTopics: Single-digit millisecond performance at any scale
Primary Key: Partition Key (simple) or Partition Key + Sort Key (composite)
Capacity: Provisioned (RCU/WCU) or On-Demand mode
DynamoDB Streams: capture item changes, integrates with Lambda
Global Tables: multi-region, multi-master replication
DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator): in-memory cache, microsecond reads, write-through
TTL: automatically expire items
GSI (Global Secondary Index): different partition/sort key
LSI (Local Secondary Index): same partition, different sort key — must create at table creation
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR): continuous backups, last 35 days
Transactions: ACID across multiple items/tables
uses: Gaming leaderboards and session management needing millisecond reads
Shopping cart data that needs horizontal scaling with traffic spikes
services.tip: NoSQL = DynamoDB. Key exam topic: on-demand vs provisioned capacity, DAX for caching.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.desc: Managed in-memory caching (Redis and Memcached).
examTopics: Redis: persistence, replication, pub/sub, Sorted Sets, Multi-AZ, backup/restore
Memcached: pure cache, multi-threaded, no persistence, simpler
Use cases: session store, leaderboards, real-time analytics, DB query caching
Lazy loading vs Write-through cache strategies
Exam trap: need persistence or Multi-AZ → Redis; simple caching → Memcached
uses: Cache database query results to serve millions of API requests
Session storage for web apps needing sub-millisecond access
services.tip: Caching layer to improve performance. Redis = more features. Memcached = simpler.

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.desc: Petabyte-scale data warehouse for analytics (columnar storage, OLAP).
examTopics: Columnar storage → fast aggregations, analytics queries
Massive Parallel Processing (MPP) across nodes
Redshift Spectrum: query S3 data without loading it
Enhanced VPC Routing: data stays in VPC
OLTP (transactions) → RDS/Aurora; OLAP (analytics) → Redshift
Snapshots: automated and manual, can copy cross-region
uses: BI and ad-hoc SQL queries on years of historical sales data
Complex analytical queries joining TB of data for executive dashboards
services.tip: OLAP = Redshift (analytics). OLTP = RDS (transactional). Know this distinction for exam.

services.name: Amazon Neptune
services.desc: Fully managed graph database.
examTopics: Use cases: social networks, fraud detection, recommendation engines
Supports Gremlin (graph traversal) and SPARQL (RDF)
Multi-AZ, read replicas, similar architecture to Aurora
uses: Social network graphs (friend-of-friend queries)
Fraud detection by analyzing relationship patterns

services.name: Amazon DocumentDB
services.desc: MongoDB-compatible document database.
examTopics: JSON documents, MongoDB API compatible (but not MongoDB itself)
Good for: content management, catalogs, user profiles
Similar architecture to Aurora (storage scales automatically)
uses: Content management systems with complex nested data structures
User profiles and product catalogs with variable schemas

services.name: Amazon Keyspaces
services.desc: Managed Apache Cassandra-compatible wide-column database.
examTopics: Use for IoT, time-series data, Cassandra migrations
Serverless, scales automatically

comparisons.title: RDS vs Aurora vs DynamoDB — When to Choose

domains.name: Networking & Content Delivery
domains.subtitle: VPC · Route 53 · CloudFront · ELB · Direct Connect · Transit Gateway

services.name: Amazon VPC
services.desc: Your private network in AWS — logically isolated cloud environment.
examTopics: Subnets: Public (route to IGW), Private (no direct internet)
Internet Gateway (IGW): allows internet access for public subnets (horizontally scaled, HA)
NAT Gateway: allows private subnet instances to initiate outbound internet traffic (managed, AZ-specific, create one per AZ)
Route Tables: control traffic routing; each subnet associated with one
Security Groups: stateful, instance-level firewall (allow rules only)
NACLs: stateless, subnet-level, support allow AND deny rules, rules evaluated in order
VPC Peering: connect two VPCs (same or cross-account/region), non-transitive
VPC Endpoints: private access to AWS services without IGW — Interface Endpoint: uses PrivateLink (ENI in subnet), most services — Gateway Endpoint: S3 and DynamoDB only (free, route table entry)
Flow Logs: capture IP traffic metadata for troubleshooting
Default VPC: pre-created, public subnets, internet-accessible
CIDR ranges: /16 to /28 allowed
uses: Isolate sensitive workloads in private subnets without internet access
Connect on-prem to AWS using VPN or Direct Connect through VPC
services.tip: Key concepts: Public vs Private subnets, Security Groups (stateful), NACLs (stateless), NAT Gateway.

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.desc: Distribute traffic across multiple targets for HA and scaling.
examTopics: ALB (Application Load Balancer): Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS), path/host-based routing, WebSockets, Lambda targets, fixed response, redirect
NLB (Network Load Balancer): Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS), ultra-high performance (millions of req/s), static IP, used for TCP traffic
GWLB (Gateway Load Balancer): deploy/manage 3rd-party virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS), operates at Layer 3
CLB (Classic LB): legacy, Layer 4 & 7, avoid in new designs
Cross-zone load balancing: distribute across AZs (on by default for ALB)
Connection Draining / Deregistration Delay: complete in-flight requests on deregistering targets
Sticky Sessions: route user to same target (uses cookie)
SSL Termination: decrypt at LB, plain traffic to targets
SNI: multiple SSL certs on same listener (ALB & NLB)
uses: Distribute web traffic across EC2 instances in multiple AZs
Health check-based routing to automatically bypass unhealthy instances
services.tip: ALB = Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS). NLB = Layer 4 (TCP/UDP, static IP). Know with Auto Scaling.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.desc: Authoritative DNS + health checking + traffic routing.
examTopics: Record types: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME, Alias (AWS-specific), MX, TXT, NS
Alias vs CNAME: Alias can point to AWS resources (free, works at zone apex), CNAME cannot be at apex

Routing Policies: — Simple: single resource — Weighted: split traffic by % — Latency: lowest latency region — Failover: active/passive with health check — Geolocation: based on user's location — Geoproximity: based on location + bias — Multi-Value Answer: multiple values with health checks
Health Checks: can trigger failover automatically
TTL: how long DNS resolvers cache the record
Private Hosted Zones: DNS within VPC only
uses: DNS with health check-based failover to a backup region
Latency-based routing directing users to the closest AWS region
services.tip: Route 53 = DNS + health checks. Routing policies: Simple, Weighted, Latency, Failover, Geolocation.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.desc: CDN — caches content at 400+ edge locations globally.
examTopics: Origins: S3, EC2, ALB, HTTP endpoint (on-prem)
OAC (Origin Access Control): restrict S3 to only CloudFront (replaces OAI)
Cache behaviors: path-based routing to different origins
TTL: default 24hr, controlled by Cache-Control headers
Invalidation: purge cache (path or wildcard), costs money
Signed URLs/Signed Cookies: private content distribution
Field-Level Encryption: encrypt specific form fields at edge
Lambda@Edge / CloudFront Functions: run code at edge
Price Class: restrict to specific edge location regions for cost savings
HTTPS: free SSL cert via ACM (must be in us-east-1)
uses: Serve static website assets globally with low latency
Stream video content to global audiences with minimal buffering
services.tip: CDN = CloudFront. Know: origins (S3, EC2, ALB), OAI for private S3, Lambda@Edge.

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.desc: Hub-and-spoke networking for VPCs and on-premises connections.
examTopics: Connects thousands of VPCs and on-prem networks through a central hub
Transitive routing (unlike VPC Peering which is non-transitive)
Cross-region peering between Transit Gateways
Route Tables on TGW for traffic segmentation
Multicast support
Replace complex VPC peering meshes with Transit Gateway
uses: Hub-and-spoke model connecting 100+ VPCs in a large enterprise
Simplifying mesh VPC peering topology to a star topology

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.desc: Dedicated private network connection from on-premises to AWS.
examTopics: Consistent bandwidth, lower latency than VPN over internet
NOT encrypted by default — add VPN over Direct Connect for encryption
Takes weeks to months to set up physically
1 Gbps / 10 Gbps / 100 Gbps connections
Direct Connect Gateway: connect to VPCs in multiple regions via single Direct Connect
Virtual Interfaces (VIF): Public VIF (AWS public services), Private VIF (VPC), Transit VIF (Transit Gateway)
uses: Consistent sub-10ms latency for hybrid apps that need both cloud and on-prem
Transferring petabytes of data with reduced bandwidth costs vs internet
services.tip: Direct Connect = private dedicated line. VPN = encrypted over internet. Direct Connect is faster/more consistent.

services.name: AWS VPN
services.desc: Encrypted IPsec VPN over public internet to AWS VPC.
examTopics: Site-to-Site VPN: on-premises to VPC via Internet Gateway or Virtual Private Gateway
Client VPN: remote employees connect to VPC
Setup takes minutes (vs weeks for Direct Connect)
Max 1.25 Gbps per tunnel (vs Direct Connect 100 Gbps)
VPN as backup for Direct Connect = common exam scenario
uses: Quickly connect a remote office to AWS VPC over the internet
Backup connectivity path alongside AWS Direct Connect
services.tip: VPN = encrypted over public internet (quick, lower cost). Direct Connect = private line (consistent, higher cost). Both connect on-prem to VPC.

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.desc: Improves global app performance using AWS backbone network.
examTopics: 2 static Anycast IPs routed to nearest AWS edge
Works at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) — compare to CloudFront Layer 7
Supports: EC2, ALB, NLB, Elastic IPs
No caching (unlike CloudFront)
Good for: gaming, IoT, non-HTTP, global users needing low latency
uses: Improve availability and performance for global gaming or fintech apps
Static IP addresses for multi-region applications behind load balancers
services.tip: CloudFront = cache content at edge. Global Accelerator = route TCP/UDP traffic via AWS backbone.

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.desc: Expose services to other VPCs without VPC peering or internet.
examTopics: Uses Interface VPC Endpoints (ENI-based)
Service provider → NLB → PrivateLink → Consumer's ENI
Traffic stays on AWS network (no public internet, no peering)
Used by AWS services themselves for private connectivity
uses: Securely access SaaS products without public internet exposure
Private inter-VPC service communication without VPC peering or IGW

callouts.title: 🪤 Critical Networking Exam Traps
items: NAT Gateway vs IGW: IGW allows bidirectional internet. NAT Gateway is for outbound only from private subnets. NAT is AZ-specific — for HA, create one per AZ.
Security Groups are stateful — if outbound allowed, return traffic allowed automatically. NACLs are stateless — need explicit inbound AND outbound rules.
VPC Peering is non-transitive — if A peers B and B peers C, A cannot reach C. Use Transit Gateway for transitive routing.
Direct Connect ≠ Encrypted — add VPN over Direct Connect for encryption.
ALB vs NLB: ALB for HTTP/HTTPS with path routing, NLB for TCP/UDP ultra-low latency or static IPs.

domains.name: Security & Identity
domains.subtitle: IAM · KMS · Cognito · GuardDuty · Shield · WAF · Inspector · Macie

services.name: AWS IAM
services.desc: Identity backbone of AWS — manage who can access which resources.
examTopics: Users, Groups, Roles, Policies
Policies: Identity-based, Resource-based, Permission Boundaries, SCPs, Session policies
Principle of Least Privilege — grant only what is needed
IAM Roles for EC2: no long-term keys stored on the instance (instance profile)
Cross-account access: trust policy + AssumeRole (STS)
Policy evaluation: explicit Deny > Organization SCP > Resource-based > Identity-based
IAM Access Analyzer: finds resources shared externally
MFA: virtual, hardware, U2F (SMS not recommended)
Inline vs Managed Policies: Managed = reusable, Inline = 1:1 attachment
services.tip: Identity-based vs resource-based policies; an explicit Deny always wins; use Roles (not access keys) for EC2 and cross-account access.

services.name: AWS KMS
services.desc: Managed encryption keys (CMKs) with envelope encryption.
examTopics: Key types: AWS managed, Customer Managed Key (CMK), customer-provided (SSE-C)
Envelope encryption: a data key encrypts data, the CMK encrypts the data key
Integrates with S3, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, SSM Parameter Store, Secrets Manager
Multi-Region Keys: replicate a CMK across regions
Key Policies + grants control who can use/manage keys
Automatic key rotation (yearly) for customer managed keys
CloudHSM: dedicated FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware you fully control
services.tip: KMS for managed keys + envelope encryption; choose CloudHSM when you need dedicated, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware you control.

services.name: AWS WAF
services.desc: Layer 7 web application firewall filtering HTTP/HTTPS traffic.
examTopics: Protects against SQL injection, XSS, bad bots, and floods
Attach Web ACLs to ALB, API Gateway, CloudFront, AppSync
Rules and rule groups; AWS Managed Rules and Marketplace rules
IP sets, geo match, and rate-based rules (rate limiting)
vs Shield: WAF = L7 application rules; Shield = L3/L4 DDoS protection
services.tip: Attach WAF Web ACLs to ALB / API Gateway / CloudFront. Use rate-based rules to throttle floods and bad bots.

services.name: AWS Shield
services.desc: Managed DDoS protection for AWS resources.
examTopics: Shield Standard: free, automatic, protects all customers (L3/L4)
Shield Advanced: paid (~$3,000/mo), adds L7 protection and 24/7 DRT
Advanced includes DDoS cost protection and WAF at no extra charge
Attach to ELB, CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator, Elastic IP
services.tip: Standard is free and automatic (L3/L4). Advanced adds L7 protection, 24/7 response team, and DDoS cost protection.

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.desc: Authentication and authorization for web and mobile apps.
examTopics: User Pools: user directory, sign-up/sign-in, JWT tokens
Identity Pools: federated identities -> temporary AWS credentials
Supports social IdPs (Google, Facebook), SAML, and OIDC
Combine User Pools + Identity Pools: authenticate, then authorize to AWS services
services.tip: User Pools = authentication (JWT). Identity Pools = federated temporary AWS credentials. Use both to authenticate then access AWS services.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.desc: Store, rotate, and retrieve secrets like DB credentials and API keys.
examTopics: Automatic rotation via Lambda (the key differentiator)
Native integration with RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB
Encrypted with KMS; fine-grained resource policies
vs SSM Parameter Store: Secrets Manager costs more but auto-rotates
services.tip: Choose Secrets Manager over SSM Parameter Store when you need automatic credential rotation.

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
services.desc: Provision, manage, and deploy free TLS/SSL certificates.
examTopics: Free public TLS certificates with automatic renewal
Attach to ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway (not directly to EC2)
Public certs validated via DNS (Route 53) or email
CloudFront requires the certificate in us-east-1
ACM Private CA for internal/private certificates
services.tip: ACM = free auto-renewing TLS for ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway. For CloudFront the cert MUST be in us-east-1.

services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
services.desc: Intelligent, ML-based threat detection.
examTopics: Agentless — analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, EKS audit logs, S3 logs
Detects compromised instances, crypto-mining, unusual API calls
Optional malware scanning
Findings -> EventBridge -> Lambda for automated remediation
services.tip: GuardDuty is agentless threat detection. Route findings to EventBridge -> Lambda for automatic remediation.

services.name: AWS Organizations / SCPs
services.desc: Centrally manage and govern multiple AWS accounts.
examTopics: OUs (Organizational Units) group accounts into a hierarchy
SCPs (Service Control Policies): maximum-permission guardrails
SCPs only restrict — they never grant permissions (even root is bound)
Consolidated Billing: single payer, volume discounts
AWS RAM (Resource Access Manager): share resources across accounts
services.tip: SCPs set the ceiling of what accounts can do — they restrict, never grant. The account root is still bound by SCPs.

services.name: IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO)
services.desc: Centralized single sign-on across AWS accounts and applications.
examTopics: Single sign-on across all Organization accounts and SaaS apps
Integrates with Active Directory and external IdPs via SAML 2.0
Permission sets assigned per account/group
Replaces creating IAM users in every account
services.tip: Use IAM Identity Center instead of per-account IAM users; federate with AD/external IdP via SAML 2.0.

services.name: AWS Network Firewall
services.desc: Managed stateful/stateless network firewall for your VPC.
examTopics: Filters traffic at the VPC perimeter (dedicated firewall subnets)
Stateful (Suricata-compatible) and stateless rule groups
Domain-name filtering and intrusion prevention (IPS)
Centralized inspection across many VPCs via Transit Gateway
vs Security Groups/NACLs: deep L3-L7 inspection, not just IP/port allow/deny
services.tip: Use Network Firewall for deep packet inspection / IPS at the VPC edge — Security Groups and NACLs only do basic allow/deny.

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.desc: ML-powered discovery and protection of sensitive data in S3.
examTopics: Finds PII, financial data, and credentials in S3
Data classification: sensitive, personal
Alerts via EventBridge or Security Hub
services.tip: Macie = find PII/sensitive data in S3 for compliance scenarios.

services.name: Amazon Inspector
services.desc: Automated vulnerability management for EC2, Lambda, and ECR.
examTopics: Scans for CVEs, network reachability, and software vulnerabilities
Continuous, event-driven scanning (Inspector v2)
Covers EC2, container images in ECR, and Lambda functions
services.tip: Inspector = continuous CVE/vulnerability scanning. Trusted Advisor = point-in-time best-practice checks (not vuln scanning).

services.name: AWS Security Hub
services.desc: Aggregated security findings and compliance checks across accounts.
examTopics: Single pane aggregating GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, IAM Access Analyzer
Automated CIS, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, PCI-DSS checks
Cross-account and cross-region aggregation
Findings in AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF) -> EventBridge
services.tip: Security Hub = central dashboard consolidating other services findings plus compliance standards.

services.name: AWS Artifact
services.desc: Self-service portal for AWS compliance reports and agreements.
examTopics: On-demand SOC, PCI-DSS, ISO compliance reports
Download AWS agreements (e.g., BAA for HIPAA)
services.tip: Artifact = download compliance reports (SOC/PCI/ISO) on demand.

services.name: AWS Audit Manager
services.desc: Automates evidence collection for audits.
examTopics: Continuously collects evidence mapped to frameworks (PCI, GDPR, SOC 2)
Turns AWS usage data into audit-ready reports
services.tip: Audit Manager = automate audit evidence collection mapped to compliance frameworks.

services.name: Amazon Detective
services.desc: Analyze and visualize security data to find the root cause of issues.
examTopics: Builds linked graphs from VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and GuardDuty
Used to investigate the root cause after a GuardDuty finding
services.tip: GuardDuty detects; Detective investigates root cause.

callouts.title: ⚠️ Shared Responsibility Model — Must Know
items: AWS Responsibility ("OF the cloud"): Physical hardware, global infrastructure, network, hypervisor, managed service underlying infrastructure, AZ/Region redundancy
Customer Responsibility ("IN the cloud"): OS patching (EC2), application code, data classification, encryption, IAM, Security Groups, network traffic, firewall config
Shared: Patch management (AWS patches RDS OS, customer patches EC2 OS), encryption (both can contribute), awareness & training

comparisons.title: Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store

domains.name: Monitoring & Logging
domains.subtitle: CloudWatch · CloudTrail · AWS Config · X-Ray · Health Dashboard

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
services.desc: Monitoring and observability for AWS resources and applications.
examTopics: Metrics: CPU, NetworkIn, DiskRead, custom metrics
Default resolution: 1 minute; High resolution: 1 second (extra cost)
CloudWatch Logs: collect, store, query application/system logs
Log Groups → Log Streams → Log Events
Metric Filters: extract metrics from log data
CloudWatch Alarms: trigger actions (ASG scale, SNS notification)
CloudWatch Dashboards: custom visualizations (cross-account/cross-region)
CloudWatch Events → now EventBridge
CloudWatch Agent: for memory/disk metrics on EC2 (not default)
Container Insights: ECS/EKS metrics
Logs Insights: query logs with SQL-like syntax

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.desc: Audit log of ALL API calls made in your AWS account.
examTopics: Who, what, when, where for every AWS API call
Events: Management Events (default, control plane) & Data Events (S3, Lambda — extra cost)
90-day event history free; persist to S3 for longer retention
Multi-region trail: captures all regions
Organization trail: capture all accounts in AWS Organizations
Log file integrity validation: SHA-256 hashing
CloudTrail ≠ CloudWatch: CloudTrail = WHO did WHAT; CloudWatch = HOW is it performing
uses: Audit who deleted a production S3 bucket at 2am
Security forensics for unauthorized IAM policy changes

services.name: AWS Config
services.desc: Configuration history and compliance checking for AWS resources.
examTopics: Records configuration changes over time (configuration timeline)
Config Rules: evaluate compliance (managed or custom Lambda)
Remediation: SSM Automation to fix non-compliant resources
Conformance Packs: collections of Config Rules + remediation actions
Config ≠ CloudTrail: Config = current state + history; CloudTrail = API calls
uses: Detect when any S3 bucket is made publicly accessible
Audit compliance: ensure all EBS volumes are encrypted
services.tip: Config = resource configuration compliance over time. Artifact = compliance reports from AWS. Don't confuse.

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.desc: Distributed tracing for microservices and serverless apps.
examTopics: Traces requests end-to-end across services
Service map: visual of microservices and latency
Segments & Subsegments: identify bottlenecks
Works with: Lambda, EC2, ECS, API Gateway, SQS
uses: Identify which Lambda function call is causing 3-second latency in an API
Visualize service dependency map for a microservices architecture
services.tip: X-Ray = distributed tracing. CloudWatch = metrics/logs. Together they give full observability.

services.name: AWS Health Dashboard
services.desc: Personalized view of AWS service health and planned maintenance.
examTopics: Personal Health Dashboard: YOUR account's affected resources
Service Health Dashboard: global AWS service status (public)
EventBridge integration: automate responses to health events
uses: Get proactive alerts about EC2 instance retirement in your account
Check if a regional outage is affecting your specific RDS instances
services.tip: AWS Health Dashboard (personal) = your resources. service.aws.amazon.com = all AWS services status.

domains.name: Migration & Transfer
domains.subtitle: DMS · SMS · Snow Family · DataSync · Transfer Family

services.name: AWS DMS
services.desc: Database Migration Service — migrate DBs to AWS with minimal downtime.
examTopics: Homogeneous (same engine) & Heterogeneous (different engine) migrations
For heterogeneous: use Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) first
Supports: ongoing replication (CDC — Change Data Capture) for minimal downtime
Source: Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, S3
Target: RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, Redshift, S3, Kafka

services.name: AWS Snow Family
services.desc: Physical devices to move large amounts of data when network is impractical.
examTopics: Snowcone: 8 TB HDD / 14 TB SSD, small, rugged, edge computing
Snowball Edge Storage Optimized: 80 TB, data transfer + edge compute
Snowball Edge Compute Optimized: 42 TB + powerful compute (vCPUs)
Snowmobile: 100 PB, shipping container on a truck, massive data center migrations
Rule of thumb: >10 TB or >1 week to transfer → consider Snow Family
All devices: encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit
uses: Transfer 500TB data center backup to S3 where internet would take months
Edge processing and data collection in oil fields with no internet
services.tip: Snowball Edge has onboard compute (EC2-compatible) for edge processing. Use when data transfer >1 week over internet.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.desc: Online data transfer service — fast migration of data to AWS.
examTopics: Sync from on-prem (NFS, SMB, HDFS) to S3, EFS, FSx
Automated, scheduled, bandwidth throttling
Preserves metadata and permissions
vs Storage Gateway: DataSync = data migration; Storage Gateway = ongoing hybrid access
uses: Weekly automated sync of on-prem file server to EFS
One-time migration of 10TB NAS to S3 before decommissioning

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.desc: SFTP/FTP/FTPS server managed by AWS, backed by S3 or EFS.
examTopics: Lift-and-shift SFTP workflows to cloud
No code changes required for existing SFTP clients
uses: Migrate legacy SFTP file exchange to S3 without changing client software
Partner file exchange using SFTP backed by S3 with IAM-based access

services.name: AWS MGN / SMS
services.desc: Lift-and-shift (rehost) server migration to AWS EC2.
examTopics: MGN (Application Migration Service) replaced SMS
Continuous replication → minimal cutover downtime
The 7 Rs: Retire, Retain, Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Repurchase, Relocate

domains.name: Analytics
domains.subtitle: Athena · Kinesis · Glue · QuickSight · OpenSearch · EMR · Lake Formation

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.desc: Serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data. No ETL needed.
examTopics: Pay per query (per TB scanned)
Supports: CSV, JSON, ORC, Parquet, Avro
Use columnar formats (Parquet/ORC) + compression = lower cost
Integrates with Glue Data Catalog (schema)
QuickSight integration for visualization
Federated Query: query other data sources (RDS, DynamoDB)
uses: Run ad hoc SQL on S3 access logs without loading them into a database
Analyze CloudTrail JSON logs with standard SQL queries instantly
services.tip: Athena = serverless SQL on S3. Pair with AWS Glue Data Catalog. No server setup — just query and pay per TB scanned.

services.name: Kinesis Data Streams
services.desc: Real-time, ordered, replayable data streaming with custom consumers.
examTopics: Sharded throughput; retention 1-365 days; ordered per shard
Custom consumers via KCL/KPL; Enhanced Fan-Out for dedicated throughput
Replay data by re-reading from a position (SQS cannot replay)
Producers: SDK, KPL, Kinesis Agent, CloudWatch Logs
Related: Kinesis Data Analytics (SQL/Flink) and Kinesis Video Streams
vs SQS: Kinesis = ordered streams + multiple consumers + replay; SQS = task queue
services.tip: Pick Kinesis Data Streams when order and replay matter, or when many consumers must read the same data.

services.name: Kinesis Data Firehose
services.desc: Fully managed near-real-time delivery of streaming data to data stores.
examTopics: Delivers to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk — no consumers to manage
Near real-time (buffer size/interval, ~60s)
Built-in transform (Lambda) and format conversion (Parquet/ORC)
No shards; auto-scales; not for sub-second or custom consumers
vs Data Streams: Firehose = managed delivery/load; Streams = custom processing
services.tip: Firehose = zero-admin load into S3/Redshift/OpenSearch. Data Streams = build your own real-time consumers.

services.name: AWS Glue
services.desc: Serverless ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service.
examTopics: Glue Data Catalog: central metadata repository (used by Athena, Redshift, EMR)
Glue Crawlers: auto-discover schema from data sources
Glue Jobs: Python/Scala Spark ETL scripts
Glue DataBrew: visual data prep (no code)
Glue Studio: visual ETL pipeline creation
uses: Transform raw JSON in S3 into Parquet for Redshift loading (ETL)
Crawl S3 data to automatically build a central schema catalog for Athena
services.tip: Glue = ETL. Glue Data Catalog = metadata store shared with Athena and Redshift Spectrum.

services.name: Amazon QuickSight
services.desc: Serverless BI and visualization tool.
examTopics: ML Insights: anomaly detection, forecasting
SPICE: in-memory fast query engine
Row-Level Security for fine-grained data access
Embeddable dashboards in apps
uses: Build sales dashboards shared across the organization from Redshift data
Embed interactive charts in a customer-facing SaaS application
services.tip: QuickSight = BI/dashboards. Athena = query. Redshift = warehouse. These three often appear together in exam scenarios.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch
services.desc: Managed search and log analytics (successor to Elasticsearch).
examTopics: Full-text search, log analytics, real-time monitoring
Often paired with Kinesis Firehose for log ingestion
OpenSearch Dashboards (Kibana equivalent)

services.name: Amazon EMR
services.desc: Managed Hadoop/Spark cluster for big data processing.
examTopics: Frameworks: Spark, Hive, HBase, Presto, Flink
Uses EC2 Spot instances for cost savings
Master/Core/Task nodes
EMR vs Glue: EMR is more control/customizable; Glue is fully managed/serverless

domains.name: Machine Learning (AI/ML Services)
domains.subtitle: SageMaker · Rekognition · Comprehend · Lex · Transcribe · Polly · Bedrock

services.name: Amazon SageMaker
services.desc: End-to-end ML platform — build, train, deploy ML models.
examTopics: Components: Studio (IDE), Ground Truth (labeling), Training Jobs, Endpoints
Built-in algorithms + BYOD (Bring Your Own Docker)
Automatic Model Tuning (hyperparameter optimization)
SageMaker Feature Store, Model Registry, Pipelines (MLOps)
Inference: real-time endpoints, batch transform, serverless inference

services.name: Amazon Rekognition
services.desc: Image and video analysis using ML.
examTopics: Face detection/recognition, object detection, text in images, content moderation, celebrity recognition
No ML expertise needed — API-based
uses: Facial recognition for employee building access control
Automatically detect and blur explicit content in user-uploaded images
services.tip: Rekognition = image/video AI. Textract = documents. Comprehend = text/NLP. Transcribe = audio.

services.name: Amazon Textract
services.desc: Extract text and data from scanned documents.
examTopics: Beyond OCR — understands forms, tables, key-value pairs
Medical: Amazon Comprehend Medical for clinical text
uses: Automate invoice processing by extracting line items and totals
Digitize mortgage applications by extracting form field data

services.name: Amazon Comprehend
services.desc: NLP — sentiment, entity recognition, key phrase, language detection.
examTopics: Comprehend Medical: specialized for clinical/medical text
Custom classification with your own training data
uses: Sentiment analysis of thousands of product reviews automatically
Extract company names and locations from legal documents at scale

services.name: Amazon Lex
services.desc: Build conversational chatbots (same tech as Alexa).
examTopics: ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) + NLU (Natural Language Understanding)
Integrates with Connect, Lambda, Kendra
uses: Customer service chatbot handling FAQs and routing escalations
Voice-based IVR system for order tracking in a call center
services.tip: Lex = chatbot. Polly = text-to-speech. Transcribe = speech-to-text. Know which does what.

services.name: Amazon Transcribe
services.desc: Speech-to-text. Convert audio to text.
examTopics: Custom vocabulary, redaction of PII, speaker identification
uses: Transcribe customer service call recordings for quality analysis
Auto-generate subtitles and closed captions for video content

services.name: Amazon Polly
services.desc: Text-to-speech. Convert text to natural-sounding speech.
examTopics: Multiple languages, SSML support, Neural TTS
uses: Add voice narration to an e-learning application
Accessibility features — read page content aloud for visually impaired users

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: Access foundation models (FMs) from leading AI companies via API.
examTopics: Provides models from: Anthropic (Claude), AI21, Stability AI, Amazon Titan, Meta
No need to manage infrastructure
Knowledge Bases for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)
Agents: orchestrate multi-step tasks
uses: Build a RAG-based knowledge assistant on internal documents
Text summarization and generation APIs for a content platform
services.tip: Bedrock = GenAI foundation models as a service. Key new exam topic for CLF-C02 GenAI domain.

services.name: Amazon Kendra
services.desc: Enterprise intelligent search powered by ML.
examTopics: Natural language search across internal documents
Connectors for S3, SharePoint, Salesforce, ServiceNow

domains.name: Containers
domains.subtitle: ECS · EKS · ECR · Fargate · App Runner

services.name: Amazon ECS
services.desc: AWS-native container orchestration using Docker containers.
examTopics: Launch types: EC2 (you manage nodes) and Fargate (serverless)
Task Definition: blueprint for container (CPU, memory, image, port)
Task = running container(s); Service = maintains desired task count
Integrates with: ALB (dynamic port mapping), CloudWatch, IAM, ECR
ECS Task Roles: IAM role for containers (best practice over EC2 instance role)
ECS Anywhere: run ECS on your own infrastructure
uses: Deploy containerized microservices at scale
Run CI/CD build agents as ephemeral containers

services.name: Amazon EKS
services.desc: Managed Kubernetes on AWS.
examTopics: Run standard Kubernetes workloads on AWS
Managed Control Plane, you manage worker nodes (or Fargate for serverless pods)
EKS Anywhere: run on-premises Kubernetes with AWS management
EKS vs ECS: EKS for Kubernetes-native teams; ECS simpler, AWS-native
uses: Run production Kubernetes clusters without managing the control plane
Migrate existing Kubernetes workloads to AWS

services.name: AWS Fargate
services.desc: Serverless compute engine for containers (ECS and EKS).
examTopics: No EC2 instances to manage — pay per vCPU and memory
Works with both ECS and EKS
Exam trigger: "serverless containers" → Fargate
uses: Run containers without managing underlying servers
Auto-scale container workloads with zero infrastructure ops
services.tip: Fargate = serverless containers. ECS/EKS still used but Fargate manages the nodes.

services.name: Amazon ECR
services.desc: Managed Docker container image registry.
examTopics: Private & public repositories
Lifecycle policies: auto-delete old images
Image scanning for vulnerabilities
Cross-region and cross-account replication

services.name: AWS App Runner
services.desc: Deploy containerized apps or source code with zero infrastructure management.
examTopics: Simpler than ECS — no task definitions, services, etc.
Auto scales, HTTPS, load balancing built-in

callouts.title: 🪤 ECS vs EKS vs Lambda — Choosing Correctly
items: Lambda: Short tasks <15min, event-driven, truly serverless, no container management
ECS + Fargate: Containerized apps, AWS-native, simpler than Kubernetes, serverless containers
ECS + EC2: Containers needing full EC2 control, GPU, special instance types
EKS: Existing Kubernetes workloads, complex orchestration needs, multi-cloud strategy

domains.name: Serverless
domains.subtitle: Lambda · API Gateway · DynamoDB · Fargate · SAM · Step Functions

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.desc: Fully managed API creation, deployment, and management.
examTopics: Types: REST API, HTTP API (cheaper, faster), WebSocket API
Integrations: Lambda, HTTP backend, AWS services, VPC Link (private)
Features: caching, throttling, usage plans, API keys, CORS
Authorizers: Lambda authorizer (custom), Cognito User Pool authorizer
Stages: dev, staging, prod with canary deployments
HTTP API vs REST API: HTTP API = simpler, cheaper, faster; REST API = more features
Edge-optimized (CloudFront) vs Regional vs Private

services.name: AWS Step Functions
services.desc: Serverless workflow orchestration using visual state machines.
examTopics: States: Task, Choice, Wait, Parallel, Map, Pass, Succeed, Fail
Standard Workflows: at-most-once, up to 1 year, auditable history
Express Workflows: at-least-once, up to 5 min, high throughput, cheaper
vs SQS: Step Functions = complex ordered workflows; SQS = simple task queuing
Error handling, retry, timeout built-in
Integrates with Lambda, DynamoDB, ECS, SNS, SQS, Glue
uses: Orchestrate a 10-step order fulfillment workflow with retries on failures
Run ML data preparation pipeline with parallel processing steps

services.name: AWS SAM
services.desc: Serverless Application Model — IaC framework for serverless apps.
examTopics: Extension of CloudFormation for Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB
sam build, sam package, sam deploy
Local testing with sam local

domains.name: Application Integration
domains.subtitle: SQS · SNS · EventBridge · SES · AppFlow · MQ

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.desc: Fully managed message queuing for decoupling applications.
examTopics: Pull-based (consumers poll the queue)
Standard Queue: best-effort ordering, at-least-once delivery, unlimited throughput
FIFO Queue: exactly-once, ordered, up to 3000 msg/s (with batching)
Visibility Timeout: message hidden after read; if not deleted → reappears (default 30s, max 12hr)
Dead Letter Queue (DLQ): failed messages after N retries
Message retention: 1 minute to 14 days (default 4 days)
Max message size: 256 KB (Extended Client Library for up to 2 GB via S3)
Long Polling: wait up to 20s for messages (cheaper than short polling)
Delay Queues: delay message delivery (0–900s)
SSE: encryption at rest using KMS
uses: Buffer order processing tasks to handle Black Friday traffic spikes
Decouple a web app from a slow order fulfillment service
services.tip: SQS = pull-based queue (consumers poll). SNS = push-based pub/sub. Often used together as SNS fan-out → multiple SQS queues.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.desc: Pub/Sub messaging — one message to many subscribers.
examTopics: Push-based (subscribers receive messages)
Subscribers: SQS, Lambda, HTTP/HTTPS, Email, SMS, Mobile Push, Kinesis Firehose
Topics: Standard and FIFO
Fan-out pattern: SNS → multiple SQS queues (highly common exam pattern)
Message Filtering: filter messages by attributes
No message persistence — delivery or dropped
uses: Send SMS/email alerts to ops teams when CloudWatch alarm fires
Fan-out: one S3 event triggers parallel processing by multiple Lambda functions
services.tip: SNS topics → push to subscribers. SQS queues → consumers pull. Key exam pattern: SNS + SQS for fan-out.

services.name: Amazon EventBridge
services.desc: Serverless event bus for routing events between AWS services and SaaS apps.
examTopics: Default event bus (AWS services), custom event bus, partner event bus (SaaS)
Rules: event pattern matching → target
Targets: Lambda, SQS, SNS, Kinesis, Step Functions, EC2 (Run Command), ECS Task
Schema Registry: auto-discover event schemas
EventBridge Scheduler: cron/rate expressions (replaces CloudWatch Events)
vs SNS: EventBridge = rich filtering, SaaS integration; SNS = simpler pub/sub

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.desc: Managed message broker (Apache ActiveMQ, RabbitMQ).
examTopics: Use when migrating existing on-prem apps using AMQP, MQTT, OpenWire, STOMP
NOT serverless (runs on EC2)
vs SQS/SNS: use MQ when you need protocol compatibility with existing apps
uses: Lift on-prem ActiveMQ broker to the cloud without rewriting app code
Hybrid cloud messaging between on-prem systems and AWS services
services.tip: MQ = for EXISTING apps using ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ protocols (AMQP, MQTT, STOMP). New apps should use SQS/SNS.

comparisons.title: SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge — Critical Comparison

domains.name: Management & Governance
domains.subtitle: CloudFormation · Systems Manager · Trusted Advisor · Control Tower · Service Catalog

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.desc: Infrastructure as Code — provision AWS resources via templates.
examTopics: Templates (JSON/YAML) → Stack → Resources
Sections: AWSTemplateFormatVersion, Description, Parameters, Mappings, Conditions, Resources (required), Outputs
StackSets: deploy stacks across multiple accounts and regions
Change Sets: preview changes before applying
Drift Detection: find manual changes made outside CloudFormation
Nested Stacks: reuse templates (modules)
Rollback: automatic on failure
cfn-init, cfn-signal: EC2 bootstrap helpers
vs CDK: CDK uses programming languages (Python, TypeScript) to synthesize CloudFormation
uses: Deploy identical dev, staging, and prod environments from one template
Version-controlled infrastructure with rollback capability on failure
services.tip: CloudFormation = IaC. CDK = define IaC in Python/TypeScript (generates CF). Terraform = third-party IaC.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager (SSM)
services.desc: Manage EC2 and on-prem instances at scale.
examTopics: SSM Agent: must be installed on instances
Session Manager: SSH/RDP without port 22 open, no bastion host needed
Parameter Store: store config/secrets (encrypted or plain)
Run Command: remotely execute commands on instances
Patch Manager: auto-patch EC2 OS and applications
State Manager: maintain desired state configuration
Inventory: collect software/hardware info from instances

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.desc: Real-time guidance to optimize your AWS environment.
examTopics: 5 categories: Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, Service Limits
Free checks: basic (6 security + limits)
Full checks: require Business or Enterprise Support plan
Common exam scenario: which tool to check for underutilized resources → Trusted Advisor
uses: Identify idle EC2 instances and unused EBS volumes to cut costs
Flag security groups with unrestricted inbound port 22 (SSH) access
services.tip: Free checks: Service Limits + some Security. Business/Enterprise Support = all checks. Exam loves this service.

services.name: AWS Control Tower
services.desc: Set up and govern a secure, multi-account AWS environment.
examTopics: Landing Zone: automated multi-account setup
Guardrails: preventive (SCPs) and detective (Config rules)
Account Factory: automated account vending machine
Built on top of Organizations, SSO, Config, CloudFormation
uses: Set up a new AWS landing zone with security baseline in hours not months
Enforce guardrails like 'disallow root user access keys' across all accounts

services.name: AWS Service Catalog
services.desc: Self-service catalog of approved CloudFormation templates.
examTopics: IT governance: only deploy approved architectures
Portfolio → Products (CloudFormation stacks)
Users can launch products without needing full CloudFormation access
uses: Allow developers to deploy only approved CloudFormation templates
Standardize EC2 configurations and enforce tagging policies via catalog

services.name: SSM Parameter Store
services.desc: Hierarchical storage for configuration data and secrets.
examTopics: String, StringList, and SecureString (KMS-encrypted) parameter types
Standard (free) vs Advanced (8 KB, parameter policies) tiers
No built-in rotation (unlike Secrets Manager)
Versioning; referenced from CloudFormation, Lambda, ECS
Public parameters: AWS-published AMI IDs, region lists
services.tip: Parameter Store = free config + SecureString secrets WITHOUT auto-rotation. Need rotation -> Secrets Manager.

services.name: CodePipeline / CodeDeploy
services.desc: CI/CD pipeline orchestration and automated deployments.
examTopics: CodePipeline orchestrates source -> build -> test -> deploy stages
CodeBuild = managed build; CodeDeploy = automated deployments
Deployment strategies: in-place vs blue/green (EC2, Lambda, ECS)
CodeDeploy lifecycle hooks + automatic rollback on failure
Sources: CodeCommit, GitHub, S3
services.tip: CodeDeploy = blue/green & in-place deploys to EC2/Lambda/ECS; CodePipeline = the end-to-end CI/CD orchestrator.

domains.name: Cost Optimization
domains.subtitle: Cost Explorer · Budgets · Pricing Models · Compute Optimizer · Cost Anomaly

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer
services.desc: Visualize, understand, and manage AWS costs and usage.
examTopics: Historical cost analysis (up to 13 months)
Forecasting future costs (up to 12 months)
Filter by service, region, tags, account
Reserved Instance recommendations
Savings Plans recommendations

services.name: AWS Budgets
services.desc: Set custom cost/usage alerts and take automated actions.
examTopics: Budget types: Cost, Usage, RI Coverage, Savings Plans Coverage
Alerts: when actual or forecasted cost exceeds threshold
Budget Actions: automatically apply IAM policies, SCPs, stop EC2/RDS when over budget

services.name: AWS Compute Optimizer
services.desc: ML-powered right-sizing recommendations for compute resources.
examTopics: Analyzes: EC2, ASG, Lambda, EBS, ECS on Fargate
Uses 14 days of CloudWatch metrics
Recommends right instance type/size to reduce cost or improve performance

services.name: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
services.desc: ML-based detection of unusual spending patterns.
examTopics: Sends alerts via SNS when anomalous spending detected
Can monitor by service, linked account, cost category

callouts.title: 💡 Cost Optimization Best Practices (Exam-Tested)
items: Right-sizing: Use Compute Optimizer to find oversized instances
Reserved Instances / Savings Plans: For predictable workloads (up to 72% savings)
Spot Instances: For fault-tolerant batch workloads (up to 90% savings)
S3 Lifecycle Policies: Move infrequent data to cheaper storage classes
Auto Scaling: Scale down during off-peak hours
Data Transfer: Keep traffic within same AZ when possible; use CloudFront for edge caching
Serverless: Pay per request (Lambda, Fargate, DynamoDB On-Demand)
Delete idle resources: Unattached EBS volumes, unused EIPs (cost money)

domains.name: High Availability & Disaster Recovery
domains.subtitle: Multi-AZ · Multi-Region · RTO/RPO · Backup Strategies · Pilot Light

cards.title: RTO vs RPO (Critical)
items: RPO (Recovery Point Objective): How much data can you afford to lose? Time between last backup and failure.
RTO (Recovery Time Objective): How fast must you recover? Time to restore service after failure.
Lower RPO/RTO = higher cost (more redundancy)
Exam: choose DR strategy based on RPO/RTO requirements

cards.title: Backup & Restore (Cheapest)
items: Backup data to S3 or Glacier
Highest RTO/RPO (hours)
Lowest cost
Restore: recreate environment from backup
Use for: non-critical systems

cards.title: Pilot Light
items: Core critical components replicated but minimally running
DB replication active; app servers off
On disaster: scale up quickly
RTO: minutes to hours
Moderate cost

cards.title: Warm Standby
items: Scaled-down fully functional copy always running
On disaster: scale up to full capacity
RTO: minutes
Higher cost than Pilot Light
Used for business-critical apps

cards.title: Multi-Site / Hot Standby
items: Full production capacity running in two regions simultaneously
Route 53 Failover or Active-Active routing
RTO: near zero (seconds)
RPO: near zero
Most expensive DR strategy

cards.title: HA Architecture Patterns
items: Multi-AZ deployments for all databases and stateful services
ELB + Auto Scaling + Multi-AZ = standard HA pattern
S3 is 11 9s durable, 99.99% available by default
Aurora: 6 copies across 3 AZs, auto-healing
DynamoDB: multi-AZ by default
ElastiCache Redis: cluster mode + multi-AZ replicas

domains.name: AWS Well-Architected Framework
domains.subtitle: 6 Pillars — Operational Excellence · Security · Reliability · Performance · Cost · Sustainability

cards.title: Operational Excellence
cards.intro: Run and monitor systems to deliver business value. Continuously improve processes.
items: Perform operations as code (IaC)
Annotate documentation

cards.title: AWS Pricing Fundamentals
items: Pay for what you use: No upfront, no long-term commitments for most
Pay less when you use more: Volume discounts (S3, data transfer)
Pay even less with Reserved: 1 or 3-year commitment
Pricing factors: compute time, data stored, data transferred OUT (inbound usually free)
Free data transfer: inbound, same-region same-service, within CloudFront edge

cards.title: AWS Free Tier
items: Always Free: Lambda (1M req/month), DynamoDB (25 GB), CloudWatch (basic metrics)
12 Months Free: EC2 t2.micro (750hr), S3 (5GB), RDS (750hr), CloudFront (50 GB)
Trials: Short-term free trials for specific services (SageMaker, Inspector)

cards.title: Support Plans
items: Basic: Free, documentation, forums, Trusted Advisor (7 checks), Health Dashboard
Developer: Business hours email support, 1 primary contact, 12-24hr response
Business: 24/7 phone/email/chat, Trusted Advisor (all checks), <1hr response for prod
Enterprise On-Ramp: TAM pool, 30min for critical
Enterprise: Dedicated TAM, Concierge support, 15min for critical, $15,000/mo

cards.title: Consolidated Billing
items: Single payment method for all accounts in an Organization
Volume discounts aggregate across all accounts
Reserved Instance benefits can be shared across accounts
Detailed billing reports per account
Management account pays for all member accounts

cards.title: AWS Pricing Tools
items: AWS Pricing Calculator: estimate costs before deployment
AWS Cost Explorer: analyze historical spend
AWS Budgets: set alerts on cost/usage
Cost and Usage Report (CUR): most granular billing data → S3
Savings Plans: flexible discount for compute commitment

cards.title: Global Infrastructure
items: Regions: ~33 geographic regions worldwide
Availability Zones: 2–6 per region (isolated data centers)
Edge Locations: 400+ for CloudFront CDN
Local Zones: extend AWS services close to large population centers
Wavelength Zones: ultra-low latency at 5G network edge
Choosing a region: compliance, latency, services available, pricing

strategy.title: 🪤 Most Common Exam Traps
items: NAT Instance vs NAT Gateway: always choose Gateway (managed, HA)
"Serverless" keyword → Lambda, Fargate, DynamoDB, Aurora Serverless, S3
EBS is AZ-locked; EFS is multi-AZ shared; S3 is globally accessible
Multi-AZ = High Availability (NOT performance). Read Replicas = performance (NOT HA)
SQS FIFO = ordered + exactly once; Standard = high throughput but not ordered
CloudTrail ≠ CloudWatch: Trail = audit WHO did WHAT; Watch = metrics HOW
SCPs do NOT grant permissions — only restrict what member accounts can do
IAM Roles for EC2: no access keys needed; use instance profile
Security Groups: stateful; NACLs: stateless (must allow both inbound and outbound)
Dedicated Instances ≠ Dedicated Hosts: Hosts give physical server visibility (BYOL)

strategy.title: 🧠 Scenario-Solving Technique
items: Identify the key requirement: cost, latency, compliance, scalability, availability
Find keywords: "serverless," "lowest cost," "HIPAA," "on-premises," "milliseconds"
Eliminate clearly wrong answers first (reduce to 2 options)
For "most cost effective" → managed/serverless + right pricing model
For "highest availability" → Multi-AZ + Auto Scaling + Multi-Region
For "security" → least privilege + encryption + monitoring + WAF + Shield
For "migration" → identify source, target, timeline, downtime tolerance
When two answers seem correct → pick the more AWS-native, managed option

strategy.title: 📅 30-Day Study Plan
items: Week 1: Compute (EC2, Lambda, ASG) + Storage (S3, EBS, EFS) + Networking basics (VPC, SG, NACL)
Week 2: Databases (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB) + Security (IAM, KMS, WAF, Shield) + Route 53 + CloudFront
Week 3: Application Integration (SQS, SNS, EventBridge) + Serverless + Containers (ECS, EKS, Fargate) + Monitoring
Week 4: Well-Architected Framework + Billing + Practice exams + Review weak areas
Take at least 3 full practice exams in the final week
Review wrong answers thoroughly — understand WHY, not just WHAT

strategy.title: ⏱️ Exam Day Tips
items: CLF-C02: 65 questions, 90 minutes (~83 sec/question)
SAA-C03: 65 questions, 130 minutes (~120 sec/question)
Mark and skip hard questions — come back later
Eliminate clearly wrong answers (usually 1–2 immediately)
Read the ENTIRE question — the last sentence often has the key constraint
Watch for "MOST cost-effective," "LEAST operational overhead," "BEST practice"
Don't overthink — if it's clearly AWS-managed and fits the scenario, choose it
Review flagged questions if time permits

strategy.title: 🔑 Services Often Confused
items: S3 Transfer Acceleration vs CloudFront: both use edge, but Transfer Acceleration is for S3 PUT/GET speed
SQS vs Kinesis: SQS = decouple, Kinesis = stream/analyze real-time data
CloudWatch vs CloudTrail vs Config: metrics/logs vs API audit trail vs compliance/history
Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store: Secrets Manager for credentials with auto-rotation
GuardDuty vs Inspector vs Macie: threat detection vs vulnerability scan vs S3 data discovery
DMS vs DataSync: database migration vs file/storage migration
Direct Connect vs VPN: dedicated physical link vs internet-based encrypted tunnel
EBS vs Instance Store: persistent network volume vs ephemeral local disk
